products.title: OVIT
products.subtitle: Deep learning–based tumor resectability prediction in ovarian cancer — a preliminary evaluation
products.description: Vision Transformer that predicts post-surgical residual tumor in advanced epithelial ovarian cancer from preoperative CT alone.

details.body:
OVIT is a Vision Transformer–based decision-support model that predicts whether a complete cytoreduction is achievable in patients with advanced epithelial ovarian cancer, using only preoperative CT scans. The architecture encodes CT slices with a pre-trained ViT and aggregates slice-level features through attention to produce a patient-level resectability score.

This preliminary evaluation, presented at Ital-IA 2024, established the feasibility of fully-automated, image-only prediction without manual segmentation or hand-crafted radiological features — paving the way for the extended journal study carried out under the UnderXAI programme.
highlights: Vision Transformer backbone with attention-based slice aggregation
Fully automated — no manual segmentation or radiological feature engineering
Validated on a cohort from the European Institute of Oncology

products.title: MESA
products.subtitle: Adapting Foundation Models for Annotation-Efficient Adnexal Mass Segmentation in Cine Images
products.description: Label-efficient ultrasound cine segmentation built on a DINOv3 foundation backbone for adnexal mass evaluation.

details.body:
MESA adapts a pre-trained DINOv3 vision transformer to the task of segmenting adnexal masses in transvaginal ultrasound cine sequences. The frozen DINOv3 backbone is paired with a Dense Prediction Transformer–style decoder that hierarchically reassembles multi-scale features, combining global semantic priors with fine-grained spatial detail.

Evaluated on 7,777 annotated frames from 112 patients across Mayo Clinic and Istituto Europeo di Oncologia, MESA reaches a Dice score of 0.945 and reduces Hausdorff distance by 11.4% over fully-supervised baselines, while remaining competitive when trained on only 25% of the available labels.
highlights: Frozen DINOv3 foundation backbone with DPT-style decoder
State-of-the-art Dice on a 7,777-frame multi-centre cine dataset
Maintains accuracy with only 25% of training annotations

products.title: CRS-ViT
products.subtitle: Vision Transformers for Preoperative CT-Based Prediction of Histopathologic Chemotherapy Response Score in High-Grade Serous Ovarian Carcinoma
products.description: Multimodal Vision Transformer that predicts the histopathologic Chemotherapy Response Score from preoperative CT and clinical variables.

details.body:
CRS-ViT is a 2.5D multimodal deep-learning framework that predicts the histopathologic Chemotherapy Response Score (CRS) — a validated biomarker of neoadjuvant chemotherapy efficacy in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma — from preoperative CT alone. Lesion-dense omental slices are encoded with a pre-trained Vision Transformer and fused with structured clinical variables through an intermediate-fusion module to produce a pre-treatment CRS estimate.

The model bridges a critical clinical gap: CRS is normally only available after surgery, but CRS-ViT delivers an equivalent score at diagnosis, when it can still inform the choice between primary debulking and neoadjuvant chemotherapy strategies.
highlights: 2.5D ViT encoder over lesion-dense omental CT slices
Intermediate fusion of imaging features with structured clinical variables
Brings a post-operative biomarker forward to diagnosis-time decision support

products.title: OVIT
products.subtitle: Deep learning for decision support in ovarian cancer treatment planning
products.description: Vision Transformer–based system that predicts residual tumor after primary debulking surgery in high-grade serous ovarian cancer.

details.body:
The extended OVIT framework is a fully-automated decision-support system that estimates residual tumor after primary debulking surgery in patients with high-grade serous ovarian cancer. Pre-trained Vision Transformer encoders are combined with an attention mechanism that aggregates slice-level evidence across the preoperative CT volume, removing the need for manual segmentation or hand-crafted radiological features.

Validated on 465 patients at the European Institute of Oncology and developed under the UnderXAI programme, OVIT delivers a patient-level resectability score together with attention maps that let oncologists interrogate the regions driving each prediction.
highlights: ViT encoder with attention-based slice aggregation
ROC-AUC of 0.80 on a 465-patient test set
Built under the UnderXAI explainable-AI programme

products.title: MedView
products.subtitle: NIfTI / DICOM viewer for VS Code
products.description: A medical image viewer for NIfTI and DICOM formats.

details.body: MedView lets clinicians and engineers inspect NIfTI and DICOM volumes inside VS Code — no separate viewer, no context switching. Useful when annotating or debugging medical-imaging pipelines.

products.title: RapidReview-US
products.subtitle: Rapid Review for Ultrasound Images
products.description: Web app for high-throughput review and classification of ultrasound cine sequences with keyboard-driven workflow and CSV auto-export.

details.body:
RapidReview-US is a lightweight Flask web app for reviewing and labelling ultrasound cine sequences at scale. It pairs full-screen playback with a collapsible classification sidebar (image class, US mode, probe orientation, ovary laterality, free-text comments) and Accept/Reject keyboard shortcuts so an annotator can move through hundreds of cases with hands never leaving the keyboard.

Built while curating the multi-centre dataset behind the MESA paper, the tool auto-saves every decision to CSV — including reviewer identity and timestamp — so the labelling pipeline is fully reproducible.
highlights: Single-key Accept/Reject workflow with frame-by-frame playback
Collapsible multi-axis classification panel for structured labels
Auto-save to CSV with reviewer and timestamp for audit trails

products.title: UNDERXAI
products.subtitle: Understanding Ovarian Cancer Initiation and Progression through Explainable Artificial Intelligence
products.description: PNRR-funded multi-centre programme building explainable-AI decision support for ovarian cancer diagnosis and therapy planning.

details.body: UNDERXAI is a multi-centre research programme funded by the European Union's NextGenerationEU initiative through Italy's Piano Nazionale di Ripresa e Resilienza (PNRR). Coordinated by NEARLab at Politecnico di Milano, the project builds an explainable-AI decision-support system to assist clinicians in diagnosing and planning therapy for patients with ovarian cancer, with explicit attention to traditionally underrepresented populations.
highlights: Co-designed with clinical partners at Istituto Europeo di Oncologia
Counterfactual and attention-based explanations for transparent decision support
Consortium across Milan, Catanzaro, Cagliari and Varese

products.title: PREDICT
products.subtitle: Predictive Response and Disease Evaluation in Ovarian Cancer with Generative AI
products.description: Generative-AI consortium that anticipates tumor progression and treatment response in ovarian cancer from baseline CT.

details.body:
PREDICT leverages generative AI to support clinicians caring for patients with ovarian cancer. The project generates post-chemotherapy CT images at diagnosis, anticipates tumor progression and predicts treatment response before therapy begins — directly targeting the diagnostic delays that drive the ~500 ovarian-cancer deaths recorded each year in Lombardy.

Funded by Fondazione Regionale per la Ricerca Biomedica (Regione Lombardia, project 012024R0055) and led from NEARLab at Politecnico di Milano with Istituto Europeo di Oncologia and Università degli Studi dell'Insubria, the consortium aims to deliver precise, personalised care strategies that reduce both diagnostic delay and mortality.
highlights: Generative AI for synthesising post-chemotherapy CT at diagnosis
Three-partner consortium: Politecnico di Milano, IEO and Università dell'Insubria
Directly addresses ovarian-cancer mortality in Lombardy

products.title: ECTR-DS
products.subtitle: Enhancing Clinical Trial Representativeness through Data Science
products.description: Cariplo-funded programme using synthetic populations and in-silico trials to improve inclusion of underrepresented groups in clinical research.

meta.funder: Fondazione Cariplo · Data Science for Health

details.body:
ECTR-DS tackles a critical limitation of randomized controlled trials: the systematic under-representation of social, ethnic and clinical minorities. The project develops data-science tools that simulate trial outcomes on synthetic populations, quantify how well a trial generalises beyond its enrolled cohort, and propose concrete strategies for broadening inclusion.

Funded by Fondazione Cariplo under the Data Science for Health call (grant 2024-0173) and led from NEARLab at Politecnico di Milano, the work combines data harmonisation, deep-learning eligibility models and GAN-based in-silico trial simulation into a unified representativeness framework.
highlights: GAN-based synthetic populations for in-silico trial simulation
Deep-learning eligibility models and harmonisation pipelines
Quantitative representativeness metrics for trial design
